proof:
# Coupled triangle cap polynomials and exact degree-six certificates

Let the actual fibers at a finite integer interval be r_k T, where
T is the standard triangle and r_k>0 are concave. Monotonicity is
allowed but is not needed for the identities below. Fix an anchor
j and its own centroid (j,(q,q)), q=r_j/3. Write z_k=k-j and
V=|T|. The proved positive-normal reduction permits an exact
minimization of its absolute cap depth using just one common normal
and one common tilt. By swapping the two continuous coordinates
and rescaling the halfspace margin, write these as

    u=(1,rho), 0<=rho<=1,
    t_k=(1+rho)q-beta z_k,
    H={x1+rho x2+beta(k-j)>=(1+rho)q}.                     (1)

No normal is minimized separately on a fiber in this note.

We prove three exact conclusions:

1. The full cap mass has a coupled difference-of-squares tail
   identity, with two nested interval supports.
2. At an interior tilt minimum a precise inequality couples the
   common normal ratio to the squared integer distances of its
   proper section fibers.
3. For rational radii, the exact own-centroid depth divided by V,
   and a realizing positive-normal cap, have algebraic degree at
   most six over Q, independently of the number of fibers. A finite
   trace-cell algorithm certifies the minimum, including all
   degeneracies and boundary normals.

These are structural and computational results. They do not prove
that some centroid reaches Gamma_2/2 for arbitrary chains, nor do
they reduce an extremizing radius profile to four fibers.

## 1. A common-normal tail identity

For 0<rho<1, put [x]_+=max(x,0). A direct triangular area
calculation gives

    |rT intersect {x1+rho x2>=t}|/V
      = [(r-t)_+^2-(rho r-t)_+^2/rho]/(1-rho)
         +(-t)_+^2/rho.                                  (2)

The four regimes of this same formula are

    r^2,                         t<=0;
    r^2-t^2/rho,                 0<=t<=rho r;
    (r-t)^2/(1-rho),             rho r<=t<=r;
    0,                           t>=r.                   (3)

Thus the exact source cap mass divided by V is

    F(rho,beta)
     =sum_k (r_k-t_k)_+^2/(1-rho)
      -sum_k (rho r_k-t_k)_+^2/[rho(1-rho)]
      +sum_k (-t_k)_+^2/rho.                             (4)

Both sampled sequences r_k-t_k and rho r_k-t_k are concave;
their positive supports are integer intervals, possibly empty.
The latter support is contained in the former because r_k>0.
The third sequence is affine before taking its positive part.
The negative sign in the second term is essential. Separate
one-sided estimates for its two squared sums cannot be inserted
with the same inequality direction without further proof.

## 2. Exact coupling on a trace cell

The lines t_k=0, t_k=rho r_k and t_k=r_k partition the parameter
plane into finitely many cells. In a cell let F0,L,H,E denote
respectively full, low proper, high proper and empty traces in
the four regimes (3). Boundary formulas agree, so a cell's formula
also extends to its closure as long as 0<rho<1.

Multiplying the exact mass by rho(1-rho) gives the cubic polynomial

    N(rho,beta)
      =rho(1-rho) sum_(F0 union L) r_k^2
       -(1-rho) sum_L [(1+rho)q-beta z_k]^2
       +rho sum_H [r_k-(1+rho)q+beta z_k]^2
      =A(rho) beta^2+B(rho) beta+C(rho).                  (5)

In particular deg A<=1, deg B<=2, deg C<=3. More explicitly, if
L_s=sum_L z_k^s, H_s=sum_H z_k^s, and H_zr=sum_H z_k r_k, then

    A(rho)=rho(L_2+H_2)-L_2,
    B(rho)=2q(1-rho^2)L_1+2rho H_zr
               -2q rho(1+rho)H_1.                       (6)

The sets and sums in these equations are determined by ONE common
pair (rho,beta). They are not freely chosen section weights.

It follows that the exact tilt curvature on the cell is

    F_beta_beta=2[rho(L_2+H_2)-L_2]/[rho(1-rho)].           (7)

An interior local minimum must have A>=0. If A>0, its tilt is

    beta=-B(rho)/(2A(rho)),
    rho>L_2/(L_2+H_2).                                  (8)

The second inequality has content whenever a proper non-own fiber
is present; A>0 itself implies L_2+H_2>0. For example, a strict
interior tilt minimum cannot have all its non-own proper sections
in the low regime. The low and high contributions have opposite
tilt curvature, even though all the individual cap masses are
nonnegative.

If A=0 at an interior local minimum, beta stationarity gives B=0.
The cap mass is then constant along that cell's vertical slice.
One can move beta to the slice's boundary without changing mass.
Thus no global minimizer is lost by considering trace boundaries
and only the A>0 stationary points in cell interiors. A<0 cannot
give an interior minimum in beta.

## 3. A uniform finite parameter rectangle

For more than one fiber choose the rational bound, when the input
is rational,

    B_* =1+max_(k!=j) (2q+r_k)/|z_k|.                     (9)

For one fiber take B_*=1. Since 0<=x1+rho x2<=r_k and
q<=(1+rho)q<=2q, at beta>=B_* every k>j fiber is full and every
k<j fiber is empty, uniformly over rho in [0,1]. The reversed
statement holds at beta<=-B_*. The own trace does not depend on
beta. Clipping beta to [-B_*,B_*] therefore preserves cap mass.

The common normal (1,rho) never vanishes. Its boundaries have
zero area in every positive triangle, so the source mass is jointly
continuous on this rectangle, including rho=0 and rho=1. Hence
the minimum is attained. Purely integer-normal closed caps are
already covered by the finite replacement in
`candidate 42889f299dc055c9`; no whole
boundary fiber is treated as null in that reduction.

At the two boundary normals the proper cap formulas simplify to

    rho=0: (r-t)^2,   0<=t<=r;
    rho=1: r^2-t^2,   0<=t<=r.                            (10)

They are full below zero and empty above r. On the corresponding
boundary trace intervals these are quadratic polynomials in beta.

## 4. The algebraic-degree theorem

Assume all r_k are rational. The finite arrangement of trace lines
inside the rectangle (9) has rational coefficients and rational
vertices. The line for k=j is included: t_j=rho r_j occurs at
rho=1/2. This avoids overlooking a vertical own-trace boundary.

First consider an interior minimizing point with A>0. Substituting
its exact tilt from (8) gives

    f(rho)=[4A(rho)C(rho)-B(rho)^2]
              /[4A(rho)rho(1-rho)]=U(rho)/W(rho),          (11)

where deg U<=4 and deg W<=3. At such a point W>0. Normal
stationarity is the single polynomial equation

    U'(rho)W(rho)-U(rho)W'(rho)=0,                        (12)

of degree at most six. When the polynomial is nonzero, its real
roots supply finitely many candidates; each is retained only if
0<rho<1, A>0 and the resulting tilt belongs to the cell closure.
All coordinates and the mass lie in the field Q(rho), of degree
at most six.

If (12) is identically zero, U/W is a rational constant. If its
stationary graph meets the cell interior, continuity and rational
density allow a rational rho in a small feasible interval, with
rational beta=-B/(2A), realizing that same constant. Thus this
degeneracy also has a rational candidate. If there is no such
interior graph, only the boundary candidates are needed.

Now consider a nonvertical trace-cell edge in 0<rho<1. It has
beta=c0+c1 rho with rational c0,c1. Substitution into (5) leaves
a numerator of degree at most three over rho(1-rho). Its normal
stationarity polynomial has degree at most four. A constant edge
value is rational and is realized at a rational interior point.
Vertical edges have a fixed rational rho and a quadratic objective
in beta, so their stationary candidates are rational. The two
normal-boundary edges use (10), also with rational quadratic
coefficients. All edge endpoints are rational arrangement vertices.

The A=0 interior case moves to an edge by Section 2. Therefore
every global minimum is attained among these finitely many
algebraic candidates, together with the rational constant values
of any feasible flat cases. The minimum of finitely many real
algebraic candidates is one of them; it is not a sum that might
increase their field degrees. This proves:

    For any finite rational concave triangle-radius chain,
    every own-centroid absolute depth divided by V has degree
    at most six over Q. A realizing cap can be chosen with
    parameters in the same degree-at-most-six number field. (13)

The candidate feasibility tests use only polynomial signs on real
algebraic numbers. Real-root isolation and exact algebraic
comparison therefore give a finite exact algorithm, including
ties. The theorem keeps every coupled normal and tilt; testing
only coordinate or all-equal normals is still invalid.

## 5. An explicit unequal-normal stationary branch

The known actual chain with radii (1/2,3/2,3/4), anchor 1, has
q=1/2. In the cell where all three traces are high proper,
the exact stationary tilt is beta=-1/8. Formula (11) becomes

    f(rho)=[33/32-(5/4)rho+(3/4)rho^2]/(1-rho).

Its unique interior local minimum is

    rho_*=1-sqrt(102)/12,
    f(rho_*)=(sqrt(102)-2)/8.                             (14)

Here 0<rho_*<1/4, so all three traces really are high proper:
the thresholds are 3/8+rho_*/2, 1/2+rho_*/2,
5/8+rho_*/2. The beta curvature is positive, and the reduced
normal function has positive second derivative. Thus this is
an actual strict local minimum of the coupled cap mass, not a
formal stationary point outside its trace cell. It is smaller
than the previously displayed rational-normal cap 81/80 because
102<(101/10)^2.

No assertion that (14) is the global minimum is required here.
The global-certificate algorithm of Section 4 explicitly also
checks every other cell and boundary. The example illustrates
why retaining the common normal produces useful algebraic
information that the independent-envelope relaxation discards.

The verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_coupled_triangle_cap_polynomials.py` checks
the exact cell identities, curvature, degree bounds and the
strict proper stationary example. It is not advertised as a
full implementation of the general cell-enumeration algorithm.
